title: Glorification
definition: Glorification is the final completion of salvation when believers are fully freed from sin and made like Christ in resurrection glory.
summary: Glorification is the final completion of salvation when believers are fully freed from sin and made like Christ in resurrection glory.
christFocus: Jesus rose in glory and will bring His people into the fullness of resurrection life with Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Glorification is the future completion of God’s saving work. The believer who has been justified and is being sanctified will one day be fully delivered from sin, weakness, corruption, and death.

This hope is bodily and eternal. Scripture does not promise an escape into vague spirituality but resurrection life with Christ, where His people will be made like Him and dwell with God forever.

Glorification shows that salvation is secure from beginning to end. The God who calls, justifies, and sanctifies His people will finish what He began through Jesus Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People living with disability, chronic pain, grief, aging, or weakness need hope that reaches beyond temporary improvement. Glorification promises that Christ will complete restoration more fully than this world can offer.

This doctrine also strengthens endurance. Present suffering is real, but it is not the final chapter for those who belong to Jesus.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Set your hope on Christ’s promised completion of salvation. Do not despise your present body or suffering, but entrust both to the Savior who will raise, restore, and make His people whole in glory.
